newsitem.title: UK: British fraud office raids Deutsche manager's home.
newsitem.headline: British fraud office raids Deutsche manager's home.

text.p: Britain's Serious Fraud Office said on Saturday it had raided the home of a former senior investment manager at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, where irregularities were exposed four weeks ago, and had started an inquiry.
The SFO said in a statement it had carried out a search at the home of Peter Young on Friday evening. It said no one had been arrested but gave no further details.
Young, 38, was sacked last week on grounds of alleged gross misconduct following the discovery of irregularities in three Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM) funds.
Trading in the MGAM funds was temporarily suspended earlier this month but resumed after a 180-million-pound ($281 million) cash injection by Germany's Deutsche Bank.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell is the London fund management arm of Deutsche Bank.

Investment watchdog IMRO and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell have been conducting their own inquiries but the SFO, which investigates and prosecutes major financial crimes, had been widely expected to take over the case.
Young has said he is being made a scapegoat. His lawyers have said there are no grounds for allegations of criminality against him.
The SFO statement said it was investigating the "conduct of Peter Young during the course of his employment by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (UK) Ltd".
A spokesman declined to say whether Young or any other persons were being questioned.
